title: Conditions Governing Suspension, Resumption and Closure of a Vending Services Program Agreement
content:
1. A client may switch the machines off without ending the Vending Services Program agreement, for a floor move, a building closure or a seasonal shutdown.
2. A suspension, a resumption or a closure is only worked while the agreement stands active, suspended or closed, and a proposal is withdrawn rather than suspended. The standing of the agreement, and the day any suspension on it began, are read from the vending agreement record before any of the three is worked.
3. A suspension shorter than the minimum printed against the programme is handled as ordinary closed days, and suspended days accumulate against the contract year ceiling printed against the same programme.
4. While suspended the standby charge printed against the programme is raised for each machine, perishable stock is removed at the start of the suspension without charge, and no commission accrues because no sales are made.
5. Switching the machines back on needs the notice printed against the programme, counted in calendar days, so that the planogram can be rebuilt and the machines refilled.
6. Only the client may end the agreement, and the desk records the request as a termination notice for the client to confirm; notice is the number of calendar days printed against the programme.
7. Where the closure day falls before the end of the term, the early termination charge printed against the programme falls due for each machine, and on or after the end of the term it does not; the collection charge printed against the programme falls due for each machine either way.
8. Commission accrued and not yet paid out is paid on closure whatever the minimum payout says, since there is no later period to carry it into.

### The standing of the agreement, condition 2 restated

| Standing of the vending agreement | A suspension, resumption or closure may be worked |
| --- | --- |
| Active | yes |
| Suspended | yes |
| Closed | yes |
| Proposed | no; a proposal is withdrawn rather than suspended |

### Closures either side of the end of the term (hypothetical dates)

Condition 7 turns on where the closure day falls against the end of the term, and the boundary is stated on both sides. A closure day falling the day before the end of the term is before it, so the early termination charge falls due for each machine. A closure day falling on the end of the term itself is not before it, so the early termination charge does not fall due; nor does it on any day after the end of the term. The collection charge is unaffected by that boundary and falls due for each machine in all three of those cases.

### What a suspension too short for the programme becomes

A suspension of fewer days than the minimum printed against the programme is not worked as a suspension at all: those days are handled as ordinary closed days. Days that are worked as suspension accumulate through the contract year against the ceiling printed against the same programme, so it is the running total of suspended days in that contract year, rather than the length of any one suspension, that the ceiling is read against.

### Charges and accruals while the machines stand off

While the estate stands suspended the standby charge printed against the programme is raised for each machine. No commission accrues over that time, because the machines make no sales. Perishable stock is removed at the start of the suspension and nothing is charged for its removal.
